title: a release comment GitHub writes and answers with a server error or with no answer at all, and lists only after the run's read of the issue's comments, stands beside the labels the run puts back, which holds the claim for good
status: fixed after 0.5.0: a run whose release comment GitHub answered with a server error or with no answer at all, and whose read of the issue's comments after it lists none, cannot tell whether the comment stands, so it leaves the labels as the release left them and counts no release of its own, as when it cannot read them, and puts the labels back only where GitHub refused the comment with a 4xx other than a rate limit's, which says it wrote nothing; since its review a rate limit's refusal, which GitHub's documentation never says comes before it acts on the call, is read as a server error is, and since its second review so is any refusal of a call the client made again after a rate limit's refusal of an earlier try (github.release_one, github.wrote_nothing, github.not_listed; DESIGN.md, 13)

steps.note: a's claim has had no commit for 25 hours, so the coordinator releases it: the labels come off, GitHub writes the release comment and answers 502, and the read of the issue's comments that follows lists none of it, since GitHub lists it only later; the run cannot tell whether the comment stands, so it leaves the labels as the release left them, counts no release and renames nothing, and the page lists the claim as held. Until the fix the labels went back, the comment then stood beside the label claimed, and the claim was held for good: every later coordinator found the comment and skipped the claim as released, and the board, seeing claimed, counted no release
the next run reads the comment GitHub now lists, counts the release and renames the branch, so #1 is in the Queue again; b's claim, idle 24 hours, is held

b's claim has had no commit for 25 hours: GitHub writes the release comment and the connection times out before any answer, and the read after it lists none of it, so again the run leaves the labels as the release left them and counts no release
the next run reads b's comment, counts the release and renames the branch

c's claim is due: GitHub answers the release comment 500 having written nothing, and the read after it lists none, which the run cannot tell from a comment GitHub lists late, so it leaves the labels as the release left them, with no comment, and counts no release; until the fix it put them back, safe here only because GitHub wrote nothing
the next run finds no release comment on #3 and releases the claim again, its labels already off counting as taken off, then renames the branch: a run more than a release GitHub refused would take

d's claim is due: GitHub refuses the release comment with a 422, which it answers in place of writing anything, and the read after it lists none, so the run puts back the labels it took off and the issue is as the run found it
the next run releases d's claim whole

d claimed #4 again at 28 hours, and its new claim is due: GitHub refuses the release comment for a secondary rate limit, asking a wait of 150 seconds, longer than a run waits, so the client tries once, though GitHub wrote the comment, as it would were canary C4 to find it acting on a call it refuses so, and the read after it lists none of it; a rate limit's refusal does not say GitHub wrote nothing, so the run leaves the labels as the release left them and counts no release. Until F23's review the run read the refusal as a 4xx that wrote nothing and put the labels back beside the comment, which held the claim for good
the next run reads the comment GitHub now lists, counts the release and renames the branch, beside the one d's first claim left

d claimed #4 a third time at 53 hours, and its claim is due: GitHub writes the release comment though it refuses it for a secondary rate limit, asking a minute's wait, which the client makes, and refuses the second try with a 422, writing nothing more, and the read after it lists none of the comment; the 422 answers the second try alone, so it does not say GitHub wrote nothing, and the run leaves the labels as the release left them and counts no release. Until F23's second review the run read the call by its last try, a 422, and put the labels back beside the comment, which held the claim for good
the next run reads the comment GitHub now lists, counts the release and renames the branch, beside the two d's earlier claims left
